page: Microsoft Azure D8ds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine hypervised via Microsoft Hyper-V, configured with 8 vCPUs derived from 4 dedicated physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture, the processor includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 260 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates comprehensive instruction support, including AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and hardware-accelerated cryptographic extensions (AES, VAES, SHA-NI). System resources include 32.0 GB of memory (maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU) and 472 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage. There are no discrete GPUs allocated to this instance.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier performance across general compute, memory, and database evaluations. Stress-ng scores show 1949.59 for single-core and 7990.62 for multi-core, reflecting average baseline throughput. In memory subsystem benchmarks, it registers 66.9 GB/sec read and 45.76 GB/sec write bandwidth on large 256 MB blocks, complementing a PassMark memory score of 2386.05. Cryptographic and compression suites reflect solid execution, with single-threaded gzip compression achieving a strong 31.31 GB/sec. Redis benchmarks show 12.02 million SET operations per second, while static web serving throughput measures 14.87 GB/sec.

The qualitative trade-off is evident when evaluating memory-bound parallel workloads and AI inference tasks. While small model inference handles prompt processing at 728.73 tokens/sec, medium 7B model text generation yields 8.03 tokens/sec, placing it in the bottom 25% due to the absence of dedicated GPU hardware. With its fast local NVMe storage and balanced memory configuration, the instance offers balanced cost efficiency for enterprise application tiers, web serving, software compilation, and transactional database workloads that do not require specialized accelerator hardware.
description: Microsoft Azure D8ds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 8 vCPUs and 4 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The platform features 32.0 GB of RAM alongside 472 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, omitting dedicated GPU hardware. CPU feature extensions include AMX and AVX-512 for vector and matrix operations, as well as hardware cryptographic acceleration. Benchmark results show average mid-range throughput across standard multi-core, single-core, and database tasks, highlighted by strong single-threaded gzip compression performance of 31.31 GB/sec and 12.02 million Redis SET operations per second. However, heavier generative AI tasks exhibit lower efficiency due to CPU-only execution. The instance delivers a well-rounded resource balance suitable for production web servers, development environments, Clang software builds, and transactional databases utilizing local temporary NVMe storage.
